text:
incident-bot: [SEV2] 502/504 spike observed at api-gateway (edge) — 15m rolling error rate 18% (> alert threshold). Paging eng-oncall.
alice: seeing the same in dashboards, spike started ~2026-03-15T09:12Z, ramped quickly. Most 502s from `edge-proxy` -> upstream `api-gw` pools.
raj: thanks. Oncall here. Can someone paste quick curl from a healthy node and one failing node? I want to see headers.
sam: grabbing logs. Quick check: head 502s have `upstream_response_time` ~0.002 but `upstream_header_time` long or missing. Also a lot of `connection reset by peer` in proxy logs.
beth: customer impact: sentry shows ~12% of production API calls failing for a subset of regions (us-east-1 and eu-west-1). Other regions OK.
paul: starting smoke tests against the gateway. `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` from a worker in us-east-1:
```
* Connected to api.edge (10.1.2.3) port 443
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< x-proxy-upstream: api-gw-2
{"error":"bad gateway"}
```
paul: same from eu-west: 504 timeout on some requests.
netops-bot: Observability: Increase in SYN_RECV and TCP_RST in edge balancer cluster eb-edge-1. No config changes in last 24h according to infra-audit.
alice: any recent deploys? CI deploy history shows a canary to api-gw cluster at 09:05Z (small rollout). Could be related.
raj: rolling back the canary now. Alice, can you confirm which revision? CLI: `rdwctl rollout status api-gw --since 09:00Z`.
alice: canary revision `api-gw@v2.7.4-canary-20260315` — initiating rollback to v2.7.3.
paul: initiating traffic switch: sending 100% of edge -> fallback pool `api-gw-legacy` to soak until rollback completes.
sam: note: metrics show an increase in concurrent connections to the pool that succeeded previously; might be a connection leak in new canary.
beth: opening status page incident (INC-20260315-01) and adding customers in affected regions with advisory: degraded availability for some API calls.
raj: rollback started. Monitoring logs for errors during rollout.
netops-bot: Rollback event detected: `api-gw` -> v2.7.3 at 09:23Z. Autoscale/no changes.
paul: after rollback, 502 rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in 2 mins, but still elevated vs baseline 0.5%.
alice: digging into proxy logs: a subset of backends still returning 502s; looks like `api-gw-2` instances have shorter keepalive and report `upstream prematurely closed connection`.
sam: I can run a targeted recycle on api-gw-2 nodes in us-east (rolling restart one at a time). Any objections? Will cause small increases in latency during drain.eth: do it, prioritize customer impact reduction. Notify if any timeouts spike.
paul: started `service restart` on api-gw-2-az1. Logs show pending connection drain then healthy.
raj: monitoring flow: looking at LB health checks — api-gw-2-az1 returned healthy after restart. Error rate fell further to 1.2%.
alice: still seeing occasional 504s from eu-west where there was heavier WAF inspection. Can we check if WAF rate limits or synchronous inspections changed?
netops-bot: WAF config last change 2026-03-10. No rolling changes today. However, traffic pattern shows 3x more long-polling requests from a small customer (~client-id x7f3) which is causing backend blocking behind proxy.
sam: isolating that client by applying rate limit on edge route `route: /v1/stream` for client x7f3 to 10r/s. Applying now.
paul: applied rate-limit; saw immediate drop in connection saturation metrics.
beth: update to customers: majority of API calls restored; small % still experiencing elevated latency/timeouts. We are actively mitigating; next update in 15m.
raj: action items: (1) finish rolling restart of api-gw-2 cluster (sam) (2) keep rollback at v2.7.3 (alice) (3) throttle abusive client for /v1/stream (sam) (4) monitor for recurrence (paul)
sam: finished rolling restart across all affected api-gw-2 nodes at 09:36Z. Confirming no restart-induced 5xx spike observed.
alice: telemetry shows error rate back to baseline 0.4% in us-east, eu-west 0.8% after throttling. Marking initial mitigation as successful.
paul: adding short-lived firewall rule to drop a small % of connections from the abusive client IP range as secondary mitigation (will document in incident timeline).
beth: are there ongoing customer escalations? Support has one open ticket (Cust-451) for higher-latency responses; pinging on resolution.
raj: bringing in SRE for post-incident review — @sre-team, please collect core dumps and heap stats from api-gw-2 nodes during the canary timeframe.
netops-bot: scheduled artifact capture: proxy pprof + tcpdump slices saved to s3://incidents/6765432100/ for 09:10-09:40Z.
alice: preliminary hypothesis: regression in connection pooling introduced in v2.7.4-canary combined with high long-poll concurrency from one client -> connection exhaustion and upstream resets.
sam: agree. Steps for follow-up: create a hotfix to revert connection pooling param changes in canary and add circuit breaker for long-polling routes.
paul: adding a temporary routing policy to prefer `api-gw-legacy` for long-poll route to avoid proxy pooling path while hotfix is prepared.
beth: status page updated: Incident -> Partial degradation resolved; monitoring. Posting post-mortem next 48h.
raj: closing immediate pager. We'll keep this thread open for timeline and retros.
alice: timeline notes: 09:05Z canary deploy v2.7.4-canary -> 09:12Z spike starts -> 09:23Z rollback to v2.7.3 -> 09:36Z rolling restart and throttling -> 09:40Z errors near baseline.
sam: leaving follow-ups: JIRA INF-2026: reproduce with client load, INF-2027: revert pool behavior in 2.7.4 and add test, INF-2028: rate-limit per-client defaults for long-poll.
beth: thanks team. I'll assign postmortem and customer comms. Reopen incident if error rate rises >2% for 10m.
incident-bot: Pager cleared for eng-oncall at 09:45Z. Incident channel archived to incident doc store.
